status: experimental Baikal shared-HDD PHY caller; no hardware acceptance

unchanged_helper.limitation: Existing readl_poll_timeout_atomic return remains ignored; rc=0 does not establish final PHY readiness.

adapted_from.interpretation: The recorded rmux source snapshot calls the Baikal PHY helper from the XHCI embedded-HDD path. This does not establish this console will work with that branch.

entry.author: rmuxnet <armandas.kvietkus@proton.me>
entry.subject: ps4: add Baikal southbridge support
entry.note: The Baikal SATA PHY setup stays immediately after pcim_iomap(); the new v7.2 ahci_validate_bar_size() call follows it.

attribution.adaptation: Meerzulee / Linux psX maintainers: Linux 7.2.11 instrumented shared-HDD probe selection, marker and Baikal-only error-path integration
attribution.license: GPL-2.0-only as declared in the preserved source header; original notices remain intact

policy_changes: Baikal XHCI shared-HDD PHY caller selects the already-present Baikal helper instead of the legacy helper.
Baikal-only AHCI initialization failure/defer propagates through pre-HCD IRQ/device cleanup only while axhci->host remains NULL (before ATA host allocation).
unchanged_policy: No helper internals, register sequences, DMA masks, IRQ allocation, NCQ, speed, timeout, retries or delays changed.
Non-Baikal PHY selection and AHCI-error handling remain unchanged.
Post-host AHCI errors retain inherited behavior; this candidate does not repair the custom-driver/libata devres lifetime mismatch.
No loader, FPKG, initramfs or boot arguments changed by this patch.

supersedes.reason: Primary review found inherited post-host libata devres lifetime handling makes broad AHCI-error propagation unsafe. Revision 2 limits the new outer unwind to Baikal errors before ATA host allocation.

lifecycle_limitations: ata_host_alloc registers ata_devres_release and ata_host_start may register ata_host_stop; both expect driver data to identify ata_host, while this custom shared driver restores axhci.

The inherited AHCI error tail can unmap/free hpriv after ATA host allocation/start. This candidate deliberately does not newly propagate those post-host errors to driver-core unwind or refactor that separate lifetime problem.
